questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
I) Abstract class can not have constructors but can have static methods.
II) A class that is declared with the abstract keyword is known as an abstract class in Java.
III) The syntax of abstract class in java is an abstract class A{}.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.answer: II, III only

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
I) If a class has multiple methods having the same name but different in parameters, it is known as Method Overloading.
II) Abstraction is the concept of defining real-world objects in terms of classes or interfaces.
III) Method overriding is a combination of inheritance and polymorphism.

Which of the above statement/s is/are correct?
questions.answer: I, II, III

questions.question: Which of the following is not true about BlockingQueue?
options: It makes it easy to implement Producer-Consumer design pattern
Has inbuilt blocking support for put() and take() methods
put() and take() methods implement LIFO ordering.
put() and take() methods implement FIFO ordering.
questions.answer: put() and take() methods implement LIFO ordering.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about deadlocks?
options: It’s a situation where all the threads die simultaneously.
It’s a situation where two threads acquire locks on the same object simultaneously.
Deadlock describes a situation where two or more threads are blocked forever, waiting for each other.
There is no such concept as Deadlock in multithreading.
questions.answer: Deadlock describes a situation where two or more threads are blocked forever, waiting for each other.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a means to avoid deadlock?
options: Using interruptible locks in the program
Avoiding nested loops and holding several locks at once
Executing foreign code while holding a lock
questions.answer: Executing foreign code while holding a lock

questions.question: Select the false statement.
options: notifyAll() method wakes up all threads waiting on the object's monitor.
wait(), notify(), and notifyAll() methods belong to the Object class.
The 'synchronized' keyword can be applied to methods and blocks.
Synchronization is a process of handling CPU scheduling.
questions.answer: Synchronization is a process of handling CPU scheduling.

questions.question: What is the correct signature of the main method in Java?
questions.answer: public static void main(String[] args)

questions.question: Which of these is a non-access modifier?
questions.answer: static

questions.question: What is the primary difference between an abstract class and an interface in Java 8+?
options: An interface can have instance variables, while an abstract class cannot.
A class can implement multiple abstract classes, but only one interface.
An abstract class can have constructors and state (instance variables), while an interface cannot.
An abstract class cannot have static methods.
questions.answer: An abstract class can have constructors and state (instance variables), while an interface cannot.

questions.question: In the Java Collections Framework, which interface provides a contract for sorting objects based on their natural ordering?
questions.answer: Comparable

questions.question: What is the difference between StringBuilder and StringBuffer?
options: StringBuilder is immutable, while StringBuffer is mutable.
StringBuilder is synchronized and thread-safe, while StringBuffer is not.
StringBuffer is synchronized and thread-safe, while StringBuilder is not.
There is no difference; they are interchangeable.
questions.answer: StringBuffer is synchronized and thread-safe, while StringBuilder is not.

questions.question: Where are local variables and object references stored in the JVM memory?
questions.answer: Stack

questions.question: What is 'type erasure' in the context of Java Generics?
options: A process where the compiler removes all generic type information at compile time.
A runtime error that occurs when a wrong type is used in a generic collection.
A feature that allows casting generic types to any other type.
The process of creating new data types.
questions.answer: A process where the compiler removes all generic type information at compile time.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the `try-with-resources` statement in Java?
options: To try multiple resources in a single try block.
To ensure that each resource is closed at the end of the statement, avoiding resource leaks.
To allocate more memory resources to the try block.
questions.answer: To ensure that each resource is closed at the end of the statement, avoiding resource leaks.

questions.question: Which Java 8 Stream API intermediate operation would you use to transform each element in a stream into another element?
questions.answer: map()

questions.question: When is a constructor called?
options: When a method of the class is called.
When an object of the class is created using the 'new' keyword.
When the class is loaded into memory.
When the garbage collector is about to destroy the object.
questions.answer: When an object of the class is created using the 'new' keyword.
